key_insight: Uniform-pressure electromagnetic pulse welding can create stronger AA1060/SUS304 dissimilar joints when it forms a wavy interface with a transition zone, combining mechanical interlocking and metallurgical bonding.
engineering_relevance: This offers a route to improve large-area aluminum–steel joining with better energy use and a longer actuator life than single-turn coil magnetic pulse welding.
method: Joined AA1060 aluminum to SUS304 stainless steel using UP-EMPW
Varied discharge voltage and initial gap to control interface formation
Characterized welds by OM, SEM/EDS, microhardness, and tensile-shear testing
evidence_signal: The best performance occurred at 9 kV and 1.5 mm initial gap, giving a mean maximum tensile-shear load of 3288 ± 256 N with failure in the aluminum base material.
watch_item: Microhardness results are useful for trend comparison, but the paper notes the indentation spacing is limited, so the hardness values should be treated as qualitative.
paper_title: Interfacial Microstructure and Tensile–Shear Properties of AA1060/SUS304 Dissimilar Sheet Joints Fabricated by Uniform-Pressure Electromagnetic Pulse Welding
